That funny little phrase deserves a place in your family’s story.

So does the bedtime voice, the blurry photo, and the letter you want them to read one day.

Meet Everlittle: a private family archive for photos, voices, stories and letters. Invite the people who know your child best to add their memories, too.

caption:
Three little things worth keeping this week:

1. The word they say in their own way. Write it exactly as they say it.
2. A familiar voice. Ask a grandparent to record a favourite song or family story.
3. An ordinary photo. Add a sentence about what happened just before it.

You don’t need a special occasion to start.

Save this for the next quiet moment.

caption:
Every family has a word that belongs only to them.

A made-up name for the dog. A funny way of saying spaghetti. The phrase that makes you look at each other and smile.

Write it down as they say it, with a little context about when they use it.

Save this prompt for tonight.

caption:
A family memory can start with a song, a photo or a familiar voice.

Record their version of a favourite song.
Add the story behind a photo.
Ask a grandparent for a voice note.

Choose whichever feels easiest today. A few words of context can make that moment even lovelier to return to.

Save these ideas for later.

caption:
A letter for your child doesn’t need a big occasion.

Try starting here:
‘You don’t have to do anything extraordinary to be loved.’

Then add one small thing you love about who they are right now. Their curiosity. Their kindness. The way they turn a cardboard box into a whole world.

Save this opening line for your next letter.
